basic_identification.name: Dataland (Refik Anadol, Spring 2026)
basic_identification.originator: Refik Anadol and Efsun Erkilic (co-founders), Refik Anadol Studio. Architecture by Gensler. Sustainability by Arup. Located within The Grand LA, a Frank Gehry-designed development by Related Companies.
basic_identification.geography: Downtown Los Angeles, at The Grand LA. Adjacent to The Broad, MOCA, Walt Disney Concert Hall, The Music Center, REDCAT, and The Colburn School.

core_ideas.core_claim: The world's first Museum of AI Arts. A permanent institution where human imagination intersects with machine creativity, establishing a new model for artistic expression at the onset of the digital age. Dataland aims to be a living space for experiencing AI art at institutional scale, not a temporary exhibition but a dedicated museum.
core_ideas.medium_specificity: Entirely digitally native in concept: a museum purpose-built for AI-generated and data-driven art. The galleries are designed for immersive digital experiences (the Infinity Room uses World Models for physics simulation). The Large Nature Model integration -- AI-generated scents from nature data -- pushes beyond visual into multi-sensory digital art. The institution itself is premised on digital art as deserving its own museum, not a department within an existing institution.
core_ideas.relation_to_attention_economy: High attention engagement. Anadol's work at MoMA attracted nearly 3 million visitors in one year. Dataland is designed for immersive spectacle -- the Infinity Room, the multi-sensory experiences, the Frank Gehry-adjacent location all optimize for visitor attention and social media amplification. The museum model depends on ticket sales and cultural buzz. However, the Artist Residency Program and Google Arts & Culture partnership suggest an intention layer beneath the spectacle.
core_ideas.relation_to_intention: Mixed. The institutional framing (museum, residency program, educational mission) signals intention: building permanent infrastructure for AI art. But the spectacle-forward design (immersive rooms, celebrity architect adjacency, luxury real estate development context) suggests attention-capture is primary. The question is whether the institutional shell can outlast the spectacle appeal of Anadol's personal brand.

market_economics.revenue_model: Ticketed museum model. Additional revenue expected from digital artwork sales (Anadol has significant track record in NFT and digital art sales). Partnerships with Google, Allen Institute. Potential merchandise and membership tiers. Located within a luxury real estate development (Conrad Hotel, high-end residences), suggesting the museum also serves as cultural amenity for property values. [uncertain]
market_economics.market_position: Institutional exhibition space. Not a marketplace but a primary exhibition venue that validates and elevates AI art. The museum creates institutional legitimacy for AI art as a category, similar to how MoMA's acquisition of Unsupervised legitimized Anadol's practice.
market_economics.price_range: Ticket prices not yet announced. Anadol's digital artworks have sold for significant sums (Unsupervised acquired by MoMA). The museum itself is positioned as a premium cultural destination in LA's museum district.
market_economics.volume_trend_2024_2026: Pre-launch. Opening Spring 2026. High anticipation given Anadol's audience (3M visitors at MoMA). The trajectory depends on whether the museum can sustain visitor interest beyond the opening period and beyond Anadol's personal practice.
market_economics.collector_demographics: Museum visitors rather than collectors per se. Expected demographic: tech-adjacent cultural consumers in Los Angeles, tourists, art-world professionals, AI/tech industry visitors. Likely to attract the Teamlab/Meow Wolf immersive-art audience as well as traditional museum-goers. [uncertain]
market_economics.sustainability: Uncertain. Artist-founded museums face sustainability challenges when the founding artist's relevance wanes. The luxury real estate context (The Grand LA by Related Companies) provides some financial backing but also raises questions about institutional independence. Revenue from tickets alone rarely sustains museums of this scale. Long-term sustainability likely depends on diversified programming beyond Anadol's own work, successful fundraising, and continued cultural relevance of AI art.

practice_aesthetics.toolchain: Refik Anadol Studio proprietary tools. Large Nature Model (open-source, trained on nature data). World Models for spatial simulation. Custom AI/ML pipelines for data visualization. Multi-sensory output including AI-generated scents. Hardware: large-scale LED and projection installations, immersive room-scale environments.
practice_aesthetics.relation_to_AI: AI is the core medium. Anadol is perhaps the most prominent artist working with generative AI as primary material. The Large Nature Model is the first open-source AI model specialized for nature data. The museum is dedicated entirely to AI arts. However, the relationship is celebratory rather than critical -- Anadol's work generally presents AI as beautiful and positive rather than examining its risks or biases.
practice_aesthetics.liveness: Generative and interactive. The Infinity Room uses World Models to simulate real-world physics in real time. Installations are dynamic, evolving, and responsive. Not static artifacts but living computational processes.
practice_aesthetics.aesthetic_vocabulary: Anadol has contributed significant aesthetic vocabulary: data painting, data sculpture, machine hallucination, AI dreams. The spectacle-scale immersive aesthetic is recognizable and influential. Critics debate whether this vocabulary constitutes genuine aesthetic innovation or decorative spectacle. The vocabulary is strong on the sublime and experiential but weak on criticality and conceptual depth.
practice_aesthetics.tendency_axis_position: Spectacle over infrastructure. Individual (artist-as-brand) over collective. Partially open (Large Nature Model) but primarily enclosed (proprietary studio tools, institutional control). The museum as institution could shift toward commons if programming broadens beyond Anadol's practice.

infrastructure_governance.openness: Mixed. The Large Nature Model is open-source. The museum itself is a private institution. Anadol's studio tools and processes are proprietary. The Artist Residency Program in partnership with Google Arts & Culture suggests some openness to other practitioners.
infrastructure_governance.governance_model: Founding-artist governed. Refik Anadol Studio controls artistic direction. Co-founded with Efsun Erkilic (business/entrepreneurial leadership). No advisory board announced. No community governance. The institution is an extension of Anadol's studio practice rather than a collectively governed space.
infrastructure_governance.data_sovereignty: Anadol/studio controlled. The Large Nature Model is trained on ethically sourced nature data, suggesting attention to data governance. However, the broader data practices of the studio (what datasets train which models) are not publicly documented. Artists in the residency program presumably retain their own IP but specifics are unclear. [uncertain]
infrastructure_governance.interoperability: Limited. As a physical museum with digital installations, interoperability is not a primary concern. The Large Nature Model being open-source enables some integration. No API, no data standards, no graph-readiness for external systems.
infrastructure_governance.preservation_strategy: Institutional archive (museum collection). The Large Nature Model on open-source platforms provides some preservation. But immersive installations depend on specific hardware and software that may not be maintainable long-term. Digital preservation of AI-generated art at museum scale is an unsolved problem that Dataland will need to address.
infrastructure_governance.consent_architecture: The Large Nature Model is described as trained on ethically sourced data, suggesting some consent framework for training data. However, details are sparse. No machine-readable consent standards. Artist residency participants presumably consent to exhibition but terms are not public. [uncertain]

field_position.relation_to_traditional_art_world: Integration through institutional legitimacy. Located in LA's museum district alongside MOCA, The Broad, Walt Disney Concert Hall. Anadol's MoMA acquisition provides art-world credibility. However, the immersive-experience model (closer to Teamlab or Meow Wolf) may position it outside traditional museum discourse.
field_position.what_it_enables: A permanent institutional home for AI art. Validates AI art as museum-worthy. Provides a model for artist-founded institutions in the digital age. The Artist Residency Program enables other artists to work with AI at institutional scale. Creates a destination for public engagement with AI creativity.
field_position.what_it_lacks: Critical distance from AI (the museum celebrates rather than interrogates). Diversity of artistic voices beyond Anadol's aesthetic. Community governance. Independence from luxury real estate interests. A preservation strategy for the art. Programming that includes AI art beyond the immersive/spectacular register.
field_position.who_is_excluded: Artists working in non-spectacle registers of AI art. Critical and adversarial AI art practices. Ticket prices may exclude lower-income visitors. The Los Angeles location limits global access. Non-visual AI art practices (text, sound, social) may not fit the immersive gallery model. Artists without relationships to Anadol's network.
field_position.frontier_signal: Frontier as institutional form. The first dedicated AI art museum is genuinely new. The question is whether it sets a precedent for institutional support of digital art or becomes a monument to one artist's practice. The Artist Residency Program is the clearest signal of broader field-building intention.

attention_intention.discovery_mechanism: Institutional presence (museum district location), media coverage, social media amplification of immersive experiences, Anadol's personal brand and audience. Partnership announcements (Google, Allen Institute) generate press coverage.
attention_intention.attention_dependency: High. The museum model depends on sustained visitor traffic, which depends on cultural buzz, media coverage, and social media virality of immersive experiences. Without attention, ticket revenue collapses. The artist-brand dependency means Anadol's personal attention capital is the museum's primary asset.
attention_intention.intention_alignment: Mixed. The institutional form (museum, residency, education) is intention-native infrastructure. But the execution (spectacle-forward, brand-dependent, luxury-real-estate-adjacent) is attention-native. The long-term test is whether the institution develops intention-serving programming beyond the spectacle opening.
attention_intention.commons_contribution: Limited so far. The Large Nature Model (open-source) is a genuine commons contribution. The Artist Residency Program could contribute to the field if it produces open research. But the museum itself is a private institution and its knowledge, curatorial intelligence, and collected works will likely remain enclosed.

provenance_temporality.provenance_type: Institutional provenance (museum exhibition history, collection records). The Large Nature Model tracks data provenance (ethically sourced datasets). Anadol's own works have blockchain provenance through previous NFT sales.
provenance_temporality.temporal_logic: Anticipatory (pre-opening, building toward spring 2026). The museum model is archival once operational. The Large Nature Model's nature data introduces deep-historical temporality (geological, ecological time).
provenance_temporality.absence_handling: Does not address absence directly. As a celebration of AI art, it foregrounds what exists (AI's creative potential) rather than what is missing (critical perspectives, excluded practices, non-spectacular AI art).

coherence.coherence_vs_consensus: Consensus around Anadol's vision. As a founder-controlled institution, it promotes a single aesthetic and philosophical position on AI art (celebratory, immersive, nature-focused). Does not yet support multiple valid readings or contested perspectives on AI art.
coherence.contestability: Very limited. No mechanism for challenging curatorial decisions, exhibition programming, or the institution's framing of AI art. The Artist Residency Program might introduce some diversity but within the institutional frame.
coherence.forkability: Low. The museum is a physical institution tied to a specific location and artist brand. The Large Nature Model can be forked (open-source). The institutional concept (AI art museum) can be replicated but the brand cannot.

adai_comparison.what_adai_should_adopt: The ambition of building permanent institutional infrastructure for digital/AI art. The Artist Residency Program as a model for supporting practitioners beyond a single artist. The Large Nature Model's open-source ethos as a contribution to commons. The demonstration that AI art can attract mass public engagement (3M visitors at MoMA).
adai_comparison.what_adai_should_refuse: The artist-as-brand institutional model. The spectacle-first, criticality-absent framing of AI art. The luxury-real-estate partnership that compromises institutional independence. The single-voice governance model. The celebration without interrogation of AI's social and ethical implications.
adai_comparison.structural_tension: Dataland proves there is public appetite and institutional possibility for AI art at museum scale. But it does so through spectacle and brand rather than through commons and collective intelligence. A(DAI) must ask whether institutional legitimacy for digital art requires this kind of spectacular capture, or whether a different institutional form -- commons-governed, critically engaged, multi-voiced -- can achieve legitimacy without spectacle. Dataland's success or failure will directly affect the credibility of A(DAI)'s alternative approach.

regulatory_legal.regulatory_exposure: Standard museum regulations. LA building and safety codes for public spaces. The AI Act may apply to AI systems used in the museum's experiences if they involve personal data processing. Copyright questions around AI-generated art are unresolved but the museum's position (training on nature data) may insulate it from the most contentious copyright disputes. Data privacy regulations apply to visitor data collection.
regulatory_legal.ip_model: Mixed. The Large Nature Model is open-source. Anadol Studio's artworks are proprietary. Residency artist IP terms are not publicly available. Museum collection rights are institutional.
regulatory_legal.opt_in_vs_opt_out: Opt-in (visitors buy tickets). The Large Nature Model's training data is described as ethically sourced, implying some consent framework. Artist residency participation is opt-in.

ecosystem.platform_dependency: Physical museum infrastructure. Depends on The Grand LA development (Related Companies) for the physical space. Technology partnerships with Google and Nvidia for computational resources. No blockchain or platform dependency. Hardware dependency for immersive installations.
ecosystem.network_effects: Moderate. The museum creates a hub effect for AI art discourse in Los Angeles. The Artist Residency Program builds a network of alumni practitioners. Partnership with Google Arts & Culture extends digital reach. But as a physical museum, network effects are limited by geography.
ecosystem.post_crash_trajectory: Not directly affected by NFT crash since Dataland is an institutional project, not a market platform. However, Anadol's practice spans both institutional and NFT worlds. The museum represents a pivot from market-dependent digital art (NFT sales) toward institutional legitimacy (museum permanence). This is arguably a post-crash strategy: building durable institutions rather than relying on market speculation.
